guide.title: Meet Diego Raúl Feliu
guide.bio_1: Diego Raúl Feliu holds a degree in Historical Tourism and has over a decade of experience bringing Panama's rich heritage to life. Born and raised in Panama City, he is a member of the Asociación Panameña de Antropología e Historia and has dedicated his career to making the nation's complex past accessible and engaging for visitors of all ages.
guide.bio_2: Whether leading school groups through the ruins of Panamá Viejo or guiding tourists through the colorful streets of Casco Antiguo, Diego combines deep knowledge with a natural gift for storytelling that transforms every tour into an unforgettable journey.

casco_plazas.title: Casco Antiguo: Plazas and Churches
casco_plazas.desc: Explore UNESCO-recognized Casco Antiguo, a living museum where colonial architecture tells the story of the nation's evolution. Visit magnificent plazas and historic churches representing Panama's journey from Spanish colony to independent republic.

details.description_1: Students step into Panama's living museum as they explore UNESCO-recognized Casco Antiguo, where cobblestone streets and colonial architecture tell the story of a nation's evolution. This immersive walking tour guides students through the district's magnificent plazas and historic churches, each representing a crucial chapter in Panama's journey from Spanish colony to independent republic.
details.description_2: 3 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Plaza Mayor, Plaza Bolívar, Plaza de Francia, Plaza Herrera
Metropolitan Cathedral, Church of La Merced, St. Joseph's Church, St. Francis Church, St. Dominic's Church, St. Phillip of Neri Oratory
National Theater, Bolivar Palace, Old Seawall

adaptations.desc: Focus on architectural features, basic historical sequence, and Panama's strategic importance.
Examine the independence movements, Bolivar's vision, and the Amphictyonic Congress.
Analyze the complex geopolitical forces behind Panama's 1903 independence and evaluate competing historical narratives from Panamanian, Colombian, and American sources.

casco_museums.title: Casco Antiguo Museum Circuit
casco_museums.desc: Students actively trace Panama's evolution from Spanish colony to modern republic through guided museum exploration tailored to your curriculum.

details.description_1: Students actively trace Panama's evolution from Spanish colony to modern republic through guided museum exploration tailored to your curriculum.
details.description_2: 3 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Engineering marvel that transformed global shipping
Colonial to republican period transition at Municipal Palace
Indigenous artistry and cultural expression
Colonial religious heritage
Historical documents, diplomatic gifts, and the Roberto F. Chiari Library

adaptations.desc: Engage with interactive displays on Panama's diverse cultural heritage and learn about Panama's independence.
Critically evaluate how Panama's strategic location shaped its historical development.
Explore how Panama's unique position created complex political and economic relationships with global powers, particularly Spain, Colombia, and the United States.

panama_viejo.title: Panama Viejo Archeological Complex
panama_viejo.desc: Step onto the excavated streets of the first European settlement on the Pacific coast, founded in 1519. Explore the ruins of this once-thriving colonial hub destroyed by pirate Henry Morgan in 1671.

details.description_1: Students step directly onto the excavated streets of Panama's original capital, founded in 1519 as the first European settlement on the Pacific coast of the Americas. This immersive archaeological site allows students to physically explore the ruins of a once-thriving colonial hub destroyed by pirate Henry Morgan in 1671. Students climb the restored Cathedral Tower for panoramic views while learning how archaeologists piece together historical narratives from physical evidence.
details.description_2: 3 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Cathedral ruins and bell tower (with optional climb)
Town hall (cabildo) foundations
Old colonial water cisterns and the convent of the Nuns of the Divine Conception
Market area and residential quarters
Plaza Mayor Museum with authentic artifacts

adaptations.desc: Focus on basic archaeological concepts and colonial life.
Examine trade networks and piracy's impact on settlement patterns.
Explore how Panama Viejo functioned as a staging area for Francisco Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire, analyzing the expedition's logistics and ethical questions surrounding colonization.

biomuseo.title: Museum of Biodiversity
biomuseo.desc: Inside Frank Gehry's only Latin American architectural masterpiece, discover how Panama literally changed Earth's biology by uniting two continents.

details.description_1: Inside Frank Gehry's only Latin American architectural masterpiece, students discover how Panama literally changed Earth's biology by uniting two continents and dividing a vast ocean. Through dynamic, interactive exhibits, students investigate how this narrow isthmus triggered one of the most significant biodiversity events in Earth's history – the Great American Biotic Interchange.
details.description_2: 2 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Surrounds students with 10 screens showcasing Panama's diverse ecosystems
Examine actual geological formations showing how volcanic activity created the isthmus
Demonstrates species migration between continents with life-sized models
Traces 15,000 years of human impact on Panama's environment
Uses twin aquariums to show how identical marine species evolved differently when separated

adaptations.desc: Focus on observable biodiversity and basic ecological concepts.
Explore species adaptation, geology, and complex biological systems.
Examine current research on climate change impacts on Panama's biodiversity. Analyze data showing how the isthmus creation altered global ocean currents and climate patterns.

miraflores.title: Miraflores Visitor Center and IMAX
miraflores.desc: Witness the engineering marvel of the Panama Canal as massive ships navigate the locks. Perfect for 4th-6th graders to observe engineering in action.

details.description_1: Perfect for 4th-6th graders, this field trip transforms abstract concepts of engineering and global trade into tangible, observable phenomena as ships weighing thousands of tons navigate the legendary Panama Canal locks. Students witness the "Miraflores Ballet" as massive gates open and close, water fills and empties, and electric "mules" guide vessels through precision operations that demonstrate core physical science principles.
details.description_2: 2 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Compare canal construction tools with modern counterparts
Identify ships passing through by country flag, cargo type, and dimensions
Observe ship transits from the observation deck
"A Land Divided, A World United" IMAX experience

adaptations.desc: Educational materials incorporate science, history, and global economics in age-appropriate formats.

religious.title: Panama's Inter-Religious Journey
religious.desc: Explore Panama's remarkable religious diversity and gain deep understanding of how different faith communities have enriched society.

details.description_1: In this unique academic expedition, students explore Panama's remarkable religious diversity while gaining deep understanding of how different faith communities have enriched our society throughout centuries. Students visit representative temples of various religions practiced in Panama, learning about the history, beliefs, and cultural contributions of these communities through direct interaction with religious leaders.
details.description_2: 4 hours of guided exploration available in Spanish and English

highlights.items: Greek Orthodox Cathedral, Kol Shearith Synagogue, Jama Masjid Mosque, Continental Bahai Temple
Hindu Temple of Panama, Soka Gakkai International Cultural Center

adaptations.desc: Analyze similarities and differences in belief systems, examine how immigrant religious communities adapted, and evaluate how different religious perspectives address modern challenges.

canal.title: Panama Canal: Miraflores Locks
canal.desc: Witness the legendary Panama Canal in action as massive ships navigate the historic Miraflores Locks—an engineering feat that changed global trade forever.

details.title: The Panama Canal Experience
details.description_1: Stand at the crossroads of world commerce and witness one of humanity's greatest engineering achievements in action. At the Miraflores Locks, you'll watch in awe as massive cargo ships and cruise liners rise and fall through the lock chambers—a gravity-defying dance of water and steel that has connected oceans for over a century.
details.description_2: Approximately 3 hours including IMAX film and lock viewing. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: Live Ship Transits
highlights.desc: Experience the thrill of watching vessels navigate the locks in real time. Your guide will explain the intricate process as ships are raised or lowered 27 feet using only gravity-fed water from Gatun Lake.

highlights.title: The Story Behind the Canal
highlights.desc: Discover the dramatic history—from the French attempt that ended in tragedy to the American triumph that reshaped global trade. Learn how Panama ultimately gained sovereignty over this strategic waterway.

highlights.title: Engineering Marvels
highlights.desc: Understand how the original 1914 locks work alongside the massive new Neopanamax locks opened in 2016, accommodating ships three times larger than the originals.

highlights.title: IMAX Theater Experience
highlights.desc: Immerse yourself in the canal's story through a stunning 45-minute 3D film narrated by Morgan Freeman, bringing the history and operation of this engineering wonder to life.

includes: Visitor center and IMAX theater admission
Optional private transportation from your hotel

casco_plazas.title: Casco Antiguo: Plazas & Churches
casco_plazas.desc: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage district where colonial plazas and historic churches reveal Panama's journey from Spanish colony to independent republic.

details.title: Plazas & Churches of the Old Quarter
details.description_1: Step into a living museum where every plaza tells a story and every church holds centuries of secrets. The Casco Antiguo—Panama's historic heart and a UNESCO World Heritage Site—unfolds before you as your guide reveals the fascinating tales behind its colonial architecture, from the grandeur of the Metropolitan Cathedral to the legendary Golden Altar of San José Church.
details.description_2: Approximately 3 hours of walking tour. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: Plaza de la Independencia
highlights.desc: Stand where Panama declared independence not once, but twice—first from Spain in 1821, then from Colombia in 1903. Your guide brings these pivotal moments to life against the backdrop of the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral.

highlights.title: The Golden Altar
highlights.desc: Marvel at the legendary altar of San José Church, said to have been saved from the pirate Henry Morgan through a clever disguise of black paint. Discover the truth behind this enduring tale.

highlights.title: Plaza Bolívar
highlights.desc: Visit the elegant square dedicated to the Liberator, surrounded by neoclassical architecture and the historic Hotel Colombia where heads of state once gathered.

highlights.title: Hidden Architectural Gems
highlights.desc: Explore the Arco Chato ruins, French-influenced mansions, and quiet corners where colonial, republican, and art deco styles blend in unexpected harmony.

includes: Optional private transportation from your hotel

casco_museums.title: Casco Antiguo: Museum Circuit
casco_museums.desc: Trace Panama's evolution through curated museum visits—from indigenous artistry to the engineering ambition that connected two oceans.

details.title: The Museum Circuit Experience
details.description_1: Discover Panama's remarkable story through its finest museums, all nestled within the historic Casco Antiguo. This curated journey takes you from pre-Columbian treasures to the audacious dream of connecting two oceans, revealing how a small isthmus became one of the world's most strategic crossroads.
details.description_2: Approximately 4 hours including museum visits. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: Panama Canal Museum
highlights.desc: Housed in the original French Canal Company headquarters, explore the epic saga of the canal's construction—from the French tragedy to the American triumph and Panama's eventual sovereignty over this engineering marvel.

highlights.title: Museum of History
highlights.desc: Journey through Panama's transformation from Spanish colony to independent nation, with artifacts and documents that bring five centuries of history to vivid life.

highlights.title: La Merced Church & Bell
highlights.desc: Visit one of Panama's most historic churches and see the original bell that was rescued from Panama Viejo after the pirate attack of 1671.

highlights.title: Indigenous Heritage
highlights.desc: Appreciate the artistry of Panama's indigenous peoples through exquisite molas, traditional crafts, and archaeological pieces that predate European contact.

includes: Comfortable walking pace with rest stops
Optional private transportation from your hotel

panama_viejo.title: Panama Viejo: Archaeological Site
panama_viejo.desc: Walk the excavated streets of Panama's original capital, founded in 1519 and destroyed by pirates in 1671. Climb the cathedral tower for panoramic views.

details.title: Where Panama Began
details.description_1: Walk through the haunting ruins of the first European city on the Pacific coast of the Americas. Founded in 1519 and destroyed by the infamous pirate Henry Morgan in 1671, Panama Viejo stands as a powerful testament to colonial ambition, indigenous resilience, and the dramatic events that shaped the New World.
details.description_2: Approximately 2.5 hours including museum and tower climb. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: The Cathedral Tower
highlights.desc: Climb the iconic bell tower—the most photographed landmark in Panama—for breathtaking panoramic views that stretch from the ancient ruins to the modern skyline, perfectly capturing 500 years of history in a single glance.

highlights.title: The Pirate Attack of 1671
highlights.desc: Stand where history's most dramatic raid unfolded as your guide recounts Henry Morgan's devastating attack and the desperate decision to burn the city rather than surrender its treasures.

highlights.title: Archaeological Discoveries
highlights.desc: Explore excavated streets, convents, and plazas while learning about ongoing archaeological work that continues to reveal secrets of colonial life and the indigenous peoples who lived here before.

highlights.title: The Site Museum
highlights.desc: View artifacts recovered from the ruins, scale models showing the city at its peak, and exhibits that bring the daily life of this once-thriving colonial capital back to life.

includes: Optional private transportation from your hotel

mi_pueblito.title: Mi Pueblito: Cultural Heritage
mi_pueblito.desc: Experience Panama's diverse cultural traditions at this living museum showcasing the architecture and customs of the country's three foundational roots.

details.title: The Three Roots of Panama
details.description_1: Journey through Panama's cultural DNA at this unique open-air museum on the slopes of Ancon Hill. Mi Pueblito brings together the nation's three foundational identities—the Campesino traditions of the Interior, the Afro-Caribbean legacy of the Canal builders, and the Indigenous heritage that predates them all—into one walkable experience that reveals how these diverse roots intertwined to create modern Panama.
details.description_2: Approximately 2.5 hours of guided exploration. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: The Pollera Museum
highlights.desc: Discover Panama's iconic national costume—considered one of the most beautiful and intricate in the world. Your guide decodes the symbolism of the handcrafted lace, the shimmering tembleques headpieces, and why a single Pollera de Gala can take a year to create.

highlights.title: Campesino Village
highlights.desc: Walk through replicas of traditional quincha houses from the Azuero Peninsula. Learn about the Junta de Embarre—the communal house-building tradition where entire villages gathered to stomp mud and straw while celebrating with music and seco.

highlights.title: Afro-Caribbean Quarter
highlights.desc: Step into the colorful wooden architecture of the Canal Zone era, including the ship-shaped Casa Müller. Understand the Gold Roll vs. Silver Roll segregation system and how West Indian workers transformed Panama's cultural landscape.

highlights.title: Indigenous Artisan Encounter
highlights.desc: Meet Guna and Emberá artisans crafting traditional molas and tagua nut carvings. These aren't mere souvenirs—molas are cosmological maps, and tagua carving is a centuries-old art form passed through generations.

includes: Optional private transportation from your hotel

biomuseo.title: Biomuseo: Museum of Biodiversity
biomuseo.desc: Inside Frank Gehry's architectural masterpiece, discover how Panama's emergence changed Earth's biology by connecting two continents.

details.title: Where Continents Collide
details.description_1: Enter Frank Gehry's only work in Latin America—a explosion of color on the Panama City waterfront—and discover how a tiny land bridge changed the course of life on Earth. The Biomuseo tells the extraordinary story of how Panama's emergence from the sea three million years ago triggered the Great American Biotic Interchange, forever transforming the biology of two continents.
details.description_2: Approximately 2 hours including all galleries. Available in English and Spanish.

highlights.title: Gehry's Architectural Vision
highlights.desc: Experience the only building Frank Gehry designed in Latin America, where vibrant canopies of folded metal evoke the tropical biodiversity within. Your guide explains how the architecture itself tells the story of Panama's natural abundance.

highlights.title: The Bridge of Life
highlights.desc: Understand how Panama's emergence created a biological superhighway. When North and South America connected, species migrated in both directions—armadillos headed north while big cats moved south, reshaping ecosystems across two continents.

highlights.title: Ocean Divided, Life Transformed
highlights.desc: Explore how the isthmus split one great ocean into the Atlantic and Pacific, creating new currents, changing climates, and isolating marine species that had once swam freely between the seas.

highlights.title: Panama's Living Treasures
highlights.desc: From the aquarium showcasing both ocean ecosystems to galleries celebrating Panama's incredible biodiversity, discover why this small nation is home to more species than the United States and Canada combined.

includes: Optional private transportation from your hotel

details.title: The Route of the Seven Churches
details.description_short: A tour through the seven most significant churches of Panama's Casco Antiguo.
details.overview_title: A Journey Through Architecture, Art, and History
details.description_1: Beyond their spiritual significance, the churches of Panama City's Casco Antiguo are the ultimate witnesses to the city's resilience. This specialized tour takes you through the seven most significant temples of the district, exploring the transition from Baroque to Neoclassical styles, the legends of treasures from the pirate era, and the architectural triumphs that defined the city's rebirth in 1673.
details.description_2: With Panama In Context, you don't just visit buildings — you decode the iconography, the art, and the social history of the religious orders (Jesuits, Franciscans, Mercedarians) that shaped the Isthmus.

churches.name: Church of Our Lady of Mercy — The Gateway to History
churches.desc: We begin at the only church whose original Baroque facade was moved stone-by-stone from the ruins of Old Panama after the pirate attack of 1671. Includes a visit to the Museum of the Order of Mercy, housing colonial documents and religious artifacts dating back centuries.

churches.name: Church of St. Joseph — The Legend of the Altar
churches.desc: Home to the iconic Golden Altar. We dive into the fascinating story of how the monks outsmarted Henry Morgan by painting the altar to hide its gold. We explore what is known, what remains uncertain, and the theories proposed to reconcile the legend with surviving historical records and the visible artistic elements of the altar.

churches.name: Church of the Company of Jesus — The Ruins of Knowledge
churches.desc: These majestic ruins represent the Jesuit legacy in Panama and the site of the first university on the Isthmus. Includes an exterior analysis of the stone masonry and the impact of the 1781 fire and subsequent earthquakes.

churches.name: Church of Santo Domingo & The Flat Arch
churches.desc: Known for its famous "Flat Arch," this site played a surprising role in 20th-century history: it was used as proof that Panama was not a high-risk earthquake zone, ultimately helping to secure political and financial support for the construction of the Panama Canal.

churches.name: Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica — The Heart of the City
churches.desc: One of the largest cathedrals in Central America. We explore its 108-year construction period, the mix of styles in its towers, and its most recent restoration for the visit of Pope Francis.

churches.name: Oratory of St. Philip Neri — The Hidden Gem
churches.desc: Often missed by tourists, this is one of the most beautifully restored peaceful spaces in the city. Includes an analysis of the delicate religious paintings, the unique courtyard reflecting the colonial monastic lifestyle, and an expansive Nativity scene (Belén) open to visitors.

churches.name: Church of St. Francis of Assisi — The Panoramic Finale
churches.desc: Located across from Plaza Bolívar, this church is a masterclass in eclectic architecture. We conclude by ascending the Bell Tower, offering the most iconic 360-degree viewpoint of Casco Antiguo and the modern Panama City skyline.

why_items.title: Expert Analysis
why_items.desc: Unlike standard walking tours, we focus on the "why" behind the architecture and the political power of the Church within the Spanish Empire.

why_items.title: Total Access
why_items.desc: Your tour includes coordinated entrance to all six restored interiors and their specialized museums, as well as the ruins of the Church of the Company of Jesus.

acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
acceptance.body: By accessing and using the Panama In Context website (panamaincontext.com), including our blog, educational materials, and tour booking services, you agree to be bound by these Terms and Conditions. If you do not agree with any part of these terms, please do not use our website or services.

intellectual_property.title: 2. Intellectual Property
intellectual_property.body:
All content on this website — including but not limited to blog articles, slide decks, infographics, videos, audio material, study guides, and images — is the property of Panama In Context and Diego Feliu, unless otherwise attributed. You may not reproduce, redistribute, republish, or otherwise use any of this content without express written consent from Diego Feliu.

Content from third-party sources (such as images from the Library of Congress) is used under their respective licenses, which are indicated alongside each item.

edu_materials_disclaimer.title: 3. Educational Materials Disclaimer
edu_materials_disclaimer.body:
Our blog articles, study guides, slide decks, infographics, and other educational materials are provided free of charge for informational and educational purposes. While we make every effort to verify all facts contained in our educational materials, Panama In Context and Diego Feliu are not responsible for any losses, damages, or consequences arising from inaccurate or incomplete information.

Each person using these materials is responsible for conducting their own fact-checking and independent verification before relying on the information for academic, professional, or any other purpose.

tour_bookings.title: 4. Tour Bookings and Payment
tour_bookings.body: Bookings for guided tours and academic excursions are not confirmed until full payment has been received. Prices are as listed on the website at the time of booking. Panama In Context reserves the right to update pricing at any time, though confirmed bookings will be honored at the price paid.

cancellation_refunds.title: 5. Cancellations and Refunds
cancellation_refunds.body: Customers are entitled to a full refund if the booking is cancelled at least 7 days prior to the scheduled date. Any bank or payment processing fees associated with the refund will be deducted from the refund amount. Cancellations made less than 7 days before the booking date are not eligible for a refund.

force_majeure.title: 6. Force Majeure
force_majeure.body: Tours and excursions may be rescheduled or cancelled due to circumstances beyond our control, including but not limited to severe weather, natural disasters, civil unrest, government restrictions, or public health emergencies. In such cases, customers will be offered a full refund or the option to reschedule at no additional cost.

photo_video.title: 7. Photography and Video During Tours
photo_video.body: Panama In Context may take photographs and videos during excursions and guided tours for promotional and educational purposes. By participating in our tours, you consent to the use of such images and recordings unless you notify us in writing prior to the tour that you wish to opt out.

liability.title: 8. Limitation of Liability
liability.body: Participants in tours and excursions do so at their own risk. Panama In Context and Diego Feliu are not liable for any injuries, illness, loss of personal property, or other damages that may occur during tours or excursions. Participants are responsible for their own safety and personal belongings at all times.

school_excursions.title: 9. School Excursions and Minors
school_excursions.body: Academic excursion bookings are made by educational institutions, not by individual students or minors. The school or institution is responsible for ensuring adequate supervision of students during excursions. Parents or legal guardians are responsible for any medical or special needs requirements, which should be communicated to us prior to the excursion.

children.title: 10. Children's Use of the Website
children.body: This website is not directed at children under 13 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us so we can remove it promptly.

governing_law.title: 11. Governing Law
governing_law.body: These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Panama. Any disputes arising from or related to these terms or our services shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of the Republic of Panama.

changes.title: 12. Changes to These Terms
changes.body: Panama In Context reserves the right to update or modify these Terms and Conditions at any time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated effective date. Continued use of the website after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

contact.title: 13. Contact
contact.body: If you have any questions about these Terms and Conditions, please contact us through our contact form at panamaincontext.com/contacto or write to Diego Feliu at diego@panamaincontext.com.

info_we_collect.title: 1. Information We Collect
info_we_collect.body:
Panama In Context collects limited personal information, only when you voluntarily provide it. We do not set cookies for tracking purposes. The information we may collect includes:

• Name and email address when you submit our contact form
• Email address when you subscribe to our mailing list
• Email address when you register for educator access to our educational materials

analytics.title: 2. Analytics
analytics.body: We use Google Analytics and Meta Pixel to collect anonymized usage data about how visitors interact with our website. This data helps us understand user journeys and improve our products and services. The analytics data collected is anonymized and does not personally identify individual visitors. It includes information such as pages visited, time spent on the site, and general geographic region.

contact_form.title: 3. Contact Form Data
contact_form.body: When you submit our contact form, we collect your name, email address, and message content. This information is used solely to respond to your inquiry and, if applicable, to provide the services you requested. We do not share this information with third parties.

mailing_list.title: 4. Mailing List
mailing_list.body: If you subscribe to our mailing list, we collect your email address to send you updates about our blog content, educational materials, and services. You can unsubscribe at any time using the link provided in each email.

educator_access.title: 5. Educator Access
educator_access.body: Educators who register for access to our educational materials provide their email address for verification purposes. This email is used to manage access to our materials and to send occasional updates about new educational content. You may request removal of your email at any time.

third_party.title: 6. Third-Party Services
third_party.body:
We use the following third-party services that may process data:

• Google Analytics — for anonymized website usage analytics
• Meta Pixel — for anonymized website usage analytics
• Payment processors — for processing tour booking payments (payment details are handled directly by the processor and are never stored on our servers)
• Sentry — for application error monitoring. Sentry receives only limited technical data about errors (such as error messages, browser type, and the page where an error occurred). It does not receive your contact-form messages, booking details, or mailing-list information.

data_retention.title: 7. Data Retention
data_retention.body:
We retain personal data for the following periods:

• Contact form inquiries: 6 months, or 3 months after any services related to the inquiry have been provided, whichever is later
• Mailing list emails: until you unsubscribe
• Educator access emails: until you request removal
• Analytics data: governed by Google Analytics and Meta Pixel retention policies

children.title: 8. Children's Privacy
children.body: Our website serves educational content for schools, but we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 years of age. Educational materials are accessed through educator accounts, not individual student accounts. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us so we can promptly remove it.

your_rights.title: 9. Your Rights
your_rights.body:
You have the right to:

• Request access to the personal data we hold about you
• Request correction of any inaccurate data
• Request deletion of your personal data
• Unsubscribe from our mailing list at any time
• Opt out of analytics tracking by using your browser's Do Not Track setting or a browser extension

To exercise any of these rights, please contact us through our contact form or at diego@panamaincontext.com.

changes.title: 10. Changes to This Policy
changes.body: Panama In Context reserves the right to update this Privacy Policy at any time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated effective date. Continued use of the website after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

contact.title: 11. Contact
contact.body: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us through our contact form at panamaincontext.com/contacto or write to Diego Feliu at diego@panamaincontext.com.
